findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookup
findings.body: When document IDs are known or tenant-local, a request can retrieve another tenant's record because `getDocument` no longer passes `ctx.tenantId` and this query filters only by `documentId`. This removes the tenant boundary enforced by the previous implementation and can disclose cross-tenant data.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module contract
findings.body: Deleting this exported module makes existing consumers of `src/cache` fail module resolution, or fail at runtime for emitted JavaScript. No replacement or compatibility export is provided despite the stated intent to preserve existing contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookup
findings.body:
Requests now query only by `documentId`. A caller in tenant A can retrieve tenant B’s document by supplying its ID, or receive the wrong document when IDs overlap across tenants.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks existing TypeScript/JavaScript consumers importing `readCached`, producing module-resolution or runtime module-not-found failures.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping to document lookups
findings.body:
In a multi-tenant database, an authenticated user who supplies another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document because the query no longer constrains `tenantId`. This removes the existing tenant authorization boundary and enables cross-tenant data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore tenant scoping to prevent cross-tenant query fan-out
findings.body:
In shared collections where document IDs are tenant-local, `db.find({ documentId })` can match one record per tenant instead of one total. Database work, result transfer, and memory consumption therefore scale with tenant count for every lookup.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
